newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela seeks to lower debt service costs.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela seeks to lower debt service costs.

text.p: Venezuelan authorities will meet with investment bankers in New York in February to discuss proposals to lower the cost of servicing the country's foreign debt, Venezuelan Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Tuesday.
Matos, who had earlier met with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus, said the meeting would take place in about two week's time.
Matos said Venezuela wanted to spread out the cost of meeting obligations on its $25 billion foreign debt, which will be sharply higher in 1997, 1998 and 1999 than in subsequent years.
"We're not talking about restructuring the debt but of changing our debt profile," he told reporters at the Venezuelan Embassy.
According to Matos, under current terms Venezuela would have to spend around $3 billion, or 40 percent, of the government's revenues every year to service the debt through 1999.
Venezuela would like investment bankers to come up with proposals that would spread out the cost of the debt servicing, roughly to around 25 percent of government revenue per year, Matos said.

The Venezuelan government is already receiving offers from investment banks, including options such as replacing its Brady bonds with other longer-term paper, along the lines of a move by Mexico last year, he said.
Venezuela will also start talks with the IMF on a program to extend its existing standby arrangement, which expires in June.
Matos said that his government has not yet decided whether it will seek an IMF extended fund facility or whether it will seek to agree on a shadow program with the fund.
Venezuela obtained a $1.4 billion IMF loan in July but only drew down around a first tranche of about $500 million.
In October, Venezuela announced it would not need the rest of the loan, pointing out that its foreign reserves had grown far more than the government and IMF had expected.
